[TAB]The Guild of Endeavors is housed in a beautiful and ornate structure, built of stone and marble, and topped by a golden dome measuring over 100 feet in diameter. An extremely difficult engineering challenge, the dome has collapsed several times during its existence. Four graceful towers stand at the corners of the building. The interior of the building is a marvelous space of columns and arches extending up to the dome, which appears almost to float atop the building. The interior is sheathed in colored marble and golden mosaics depicting legendary scenes and images of kings.

[TAB]If a wild animal is captured it can be taken to a city with a [LINK=BUILDING_CARNIVAL]Carnival[\\LINK] and added to the city as an attraction. This raises both the [ICON_CULTURE] and [ICON_HAPPY] effects of the Carnival. Enough of these attractions will permit the construction of the [LINK=BUILDING_GRAND_MENAGERIE]Grand Menagerie[\\LINK].

[TAB]The Balseraphs do not only display lesser animals for entertainment in their [LINK=BUILDING_CARNIVAL]Carnivals[\\LINK], but also slaves of the intelligent races. Balseraph players may sacrifice a slave of each different race in order to create an exhibit in a city with a [LINK=BUILDING_FREAK_SHOW]Freak Show[\\LINK]. These raise the [ICON_CULTURE], [ICON_HAPPY], and Great Person Points for Artists in the city. They also count towards the number of attractions which a city must have in order to house the [LINK=BUILDING_GRAND_MENAGERIE]Grand Menagerie[\\LINK].

Arawn is often called the Unhearing God, because he ignores all the prayers. of his worshipers in Creation, occupying himself with the matters of the afterworld instead. Despite this a small cult called The Eternal Cabal choose to worship him, though it is as useful as worshiping a rock. Occasionally the Archangel Gyra has intervened to help those who worship her god, although she is usually too busy battling the forces of Laroth. Many who believe they follow Arawn have actually been deceived into serving the Haunted, agents of Laroth who worship him as the new God of Death.

[TAB]Once the Mercurian Gate is completed the Mercurians may enter the world and join the side of whoever built the gate. [PARAGRAPH:1]The Player that builds this wonder will have the option of abandoning control of his civilization and taking control of the Mercurians instead. [PARAGRAPH:1]The Mercurians are angels, but angels with only one purpose, to destroy the legions of hell. They care little for the means required to achieve that end, and will battle as loyally beside the cruel Calabim as they will the compassionate Elohim, as long as the Infernal remains their common enemy.

Unlike in normal Fall from Heaven 2, a player who completes this wonder does not automatically cede control of the city of %s1 to the Mercurian civilization. Basium may choose to take some cities from his AI teammates without their permission, but from human allies he will only take what is gifted through diplomacy. [PARAGRAPH:1] The Mercurians are not summoned by the Mercurian Gate itself, but by the Open Mercurian Gate spell which it allows. [PARAGRAPH:1] Once Basium (the unit) is dead it also allows the Call Mercurian Reinforcements spell, which resurrects Basium along with another army of Angels. The Mercurians cannot use this ability themselves. The player that does use this ability gets a diplomatic bonus with Basium and makes peace with him if they were at war. Players who follow The Ashen Veil cannot use this ability either. [PARAGRAPH:1]This is now a National Wonder rather than a World Wonder. Each team may build one and may rebuild it if they loose it, but not while Basium (the unit) is alive. [PARAGRAPH:1]The cost of the gate can vary. It scales with the percent influence of The Ashen Veil religion. Being at war with an Infernal player or a player with The Ashen Veil state religion makes it cheaper. It also becomes cheaper if your enemies use evil spheres of magic (Entropy, Dimensional, Chaos, Death) and more expensive if your own team uses them.
